trades.headline: Cash in Josh Downs' trade bump and Kirk Cousins' hot streak for DeVonta Smith's new WR1 role
trades.summary: Josh Downs and Kirk Cousins are both priced off recent hype that likely fades; DeVonta Smith just became Philadelphia's top target with A.J. Brown gone.

give: Downs' value is up 192% in 30 days purely off his trade from Indianapolis to Kansas City; he's not even guaranteed every-down snaps there yet (69% snap, 19% target share)
Cousins is a 38-year-old journeyman just plugged in after a Week 10 trade from Las Vegas, with Minnesota having already benched two other QBs (Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz) this season
get: Smith has taken over as Philadelphia's top target (36% target share, 85% snaps) since A.J. Brown left; his 30-day value dip (-19%) reflects box-score results, not his role
He's outproducing his projection on a per-target basis (1.09 perf) even while the 30-day trend lags the role change
you: Smith slots straight into your FLEX in place of Downs with a clearly bigger role
Clears a crowded bench QB spot (Cousins) you can't start behind Jayden Daniels
them: Mad Cows are 7-4 and pushing for a playoff spot; Cousins gives them immediate QB depth or a bridge option, and Downs is a buy-low flier on a Chiefs offense trending up
They're already deep at WR and RB, so moving one WR piece (Smith) for immediate QB/WR depth costs them little
experts: FantasyPros' 2026 outlook notes Smith has moved into Philadelphia's top receiver role since Brown's departure, roughly a third of the team's targets (fantasypros.com)
Analysts see Downs' trade to Kansas City as an upgrade in QB play, but caution patience is needed as his role with the Chiefs settles (clutchpoints.com, fantasylife.com)

Cousins was a surprise Week 10 trade acquisition and was only named Minnesota's starter after Carson Wentz struggled; the Vikings have already cycled through three different QB plans this season (mprnews.org, tsn.ca)

risks: If Smith's early-down role doesn't hold once Philadelphia's offense gets fully healthy, the target-share gain shrinks
Cousins could put together a hot stretch before cooling off, making the sell look early

trades.headline: Flip a hot flex receiver for a tight end who's still just getting back up to speed
trades.summary: Stefon Diggs is playing above his projection right now; Tucker Kraft is a year removed from a torn ACL and still working back to his snap share without the production to match yet.

give: Diggs is beating his projection (1.15 perf, +14% 30-day value) on a lower target share (22%) than his price implies — due for a correction
get: Kraft's snaps are back to normal (83%) after his torn ACL, but his catch rate and scoring haven't caught up yet, which is why his value has dropped 40% in 30 days
A fantasy outlook published this year says a fully healthy Kraft has a realistic path to a top-three tight end finish
you: Kraft replaces Juwan Johnson as your starting tight end, a clear upgrade at a thin position
DK Metcalf moves into the FLEX spot Diggs vacates, so you're not actually losing a starter
them: ChampaignTornadoes are 7-4 and deep at WR/RB already; adding a proven, healthy flex receiver now matters more to them than keeping a TE still working back from injury
Lamar Jackson evens the value and costs them nothing of consequence at a position where they're already set
experts: A midseason recap notes Kraft 'flops as Packers WRs exploded,' underscoring that the ball isn't finding him yet even though he's playing nearly every snap (draftsharks.com)
PFF's 2026 outlook piece frames a healthy Kraft as a potential top-three fantasy tight end once he's fully back (pff.com)

risks: If Green Bay's passing game keeps funneling targets to its receivers instead of Kraft, his price may not recover this season
Diggs could keep running hot if his big-play role expands further

trades.headline: Package bench depth to fix your thin tight end spot with Kyle Pitts
trades.summary: Pat Bryant and Juwan Johnson are both fringe roster pieces; Kyle Pitts is a clear starting upgrade at tight end even in a middling Atlanta passing game.

give: Johnson is your current starting tight end but is averaging under his projection (0.84 perf) with a declining role (30-day value -69%)
Bryant is a WR4/5 piece buried on your bench with a 59% snap share and modest target volume
get: Pitts remains Atlanta's clear complementary pass-catching option behind Drake London even as the offense has scuffled
His price (528) reflects years of up-and-down target volume more than a change in his week-to-week role
you: Pitts becomes your starting tight end in place of Johnson, directly fixing your thin TE spot
You give up only bench pieces (Bryant, Johnson) that weren't starting for you anyway
them: Ben Hur Returns are 2-9 and can afford to let Pitts go for a younger value add (Bryant) while clearing a roster spot
Devaughn Vele is a depth throw-in for them that costs little
experts: CBS Sports' ongoing fantasy news coverage of Atlanta's passing game continues to list Pitts as a week-to-week complementary receiving option behind London, with inconsistent weekly catch totals (cbssports.com)

risks: Pitts has disappointed fantasy managers for multiple seasons running, so there's real downside he stays a low-ceiling TE2
If Atlanta's offense keeps sputtering, his weekly target count may not grow

trades.headline: A second path to the same tight end fix: Dallas Goedert instead of Pitts
trades.summary: Goedert is PFF's No. 2 graded tight end this season but still priced like a replacement-level option; a late bench piece and a buried backup QB get it done.

give: Bryant is a bench WR with limited snaps and no clear path to your starting lineup
McGowan is a deep bench RB (23% snap share) you're not starting
get: Goedert carries an 80.0 PFF grade this season, 2nd among all qualified tight ends, yet is valued at only 512 — well under where that level of play usually prices
He's stayed productive and relevant even through an Eagles QB change this season
you: Goedert becomes your clear starting tight end upgrade over Johnson
You part with only bench players who weren't in your lineup
them: Urbana Rattlesnakes are 10-1 and flush at TE/RB; moving a TE they can spare for bench pieces that round out their roster costs them little at the position they need least
J.J. McCarthy is a buried backup QB for them with no path to playing time behind Minnesota's current starter, so it's a low-cost throw-in
experts: PFF grades Goedert 80.0 overall this season, 2nd among 30 qualified tight ends (pff.com)
A midseason Draftsharks piece is headlined 'Dallas Goedert stays useful amid QB shift,' underscoring his role has held up through quarterback turnover in Philadelphia (draftsharks.com)

risks: Goedert has battled durability issues throughout his career, so there's always an injury risk
If Philadelphia leans run-heavy down the stretch, his target count could stay capped

sources.title: Dallas Goedert stays useful amid QB shift

trades.headline: Spend from your deep WR room to land an elite buy-low tight end and another receiver
trades.summary: You're overloaded at receiver; Malik Nabers and a sold-high Josh Downs convert into Trey McBride, fantasy's TE1 last year now priced down, plus a rising Tampa Bay receiver.

give: Nabers is a true alpha WR but you're deep at the position with Wilson, Diggs, Metcalf and Brown also rostered
Downs is priced up 192% in 30 days purely from his trade hype (see trade with Mad Cows for detail)
get: McBride still commands a 29% target share and 90% snaps as Arizona's clear top receiving option, and his -12% value dip looks like noise against that role
Egbuka is stepping into a bigger role in Tampa Bay with Mike Evans gone, and his 24% target share and 83% snaps haven't caught up to his price yet (-38% in 30 days)
you: McBride fixes your thin TE spot as an outright starter, and Egbuka also moves into your starting lineup; DK Metcalf slides into your remaining FLEX spot
You're selling from a position of WR surplus rather than weakening your own lineup
them: Lightning Struyks Twice are 6-5 and thin at WR/QB; adding a true WR1 in Nabers directly fills their biggest hole
They're deep at TE/RB, so moving McBride for a bigger receiver upgrade is a reasonable value swap for a team chasing a playoff spot
experts: FantasyPros' mid-2026 outlook ranks McBride first among 59 qualified tight ends with a 25.4% target share (fantasypros.com)
Coverage of Tampa Bay's 2026 season says Egbuka is 'primed for an even more significant role' with Mike Evans no longer on the roster (nbcsports.com, upi.com)

risks: Giving up Nabers means trading a true top-10 WR; this only makes sense if your WR depth truly goes unused in your lineup
Egbuka missed time with a hamstring injury last season; he carries no current injury designation, but it's worth a fresh check before and after the deal

sources.title: Depleted Bucs lose WR Emeka Egbuka to hamstring injury

trades.headline: Swap a timeshare rookie RB and a hot backup QB for a settled TE1 and a featured Vikings back
trades.summary: Quinshon Judkins is stuck in an unresolved Cleveland backfield timeshare; Sam LaPorta and Aaron Jones Sr. both keep full-time roles despite their recent dips.

give: Judkins is splitting carries with Dylan Sampson in what's been described as a developing timeshare, with reports this season of his snap count varying week to week on 'situational' grounds
Cousins is a short-term Vikings starter just installed after the team benched two other QBs this season (see Mad Cows trade for detail)
get: LaPorta remains Detroit's top pass-catching tight end (89% snaps, 18% target share); he's currently listed Questionable, so confirm his status before pulling the trigger
Jones has played through a knee issue this season and still logs 15.2 touches per game as Minnesota's lead back, even as his price dropped 36% in 30 days
you: LaPorta becomes your starting tight end over Johnson, and Jones steps into your lineup at RB
You're not giving up a settled role at RB — Judkins' snaps have been unpredictable all season
them: Inverness Hissing Iguanas are 7-4 and already deep at RB; adding Judkins gives them a younger piece while moving on from a TE spot that's been banged up
They get a QB-needy sweetener in Cousins at no real cost to their roster
experts: A CBS Sports report notes the Browns backfield could be 'drifting toward a timeshare' between Judkins and Sampson as the staff looks for solutions
Jones suffered a knee injury in Minnesota's Oct. 25 win over the Colts this season, got good news on it days later, and has kept his workload since (thevikingage.com)

risks: If Sampson's role shrinks instead of Judkins', this looks like selling too early on the better back
LaPorta's current Questionable tag and Jones' knee injury both bear watching before locking in the trade
